question: Should `scripts/pr` permanently reject all prepare and merge commands for non-main PRs and require the separate reviewed release-branch landing flow?
rationale: The guard prevents a demonstrated unsafe rebase onto main, but it also changes an operator-facing command contract and may block release workflows that previously reached later stages.

options.title: Keep the strict boundary
options.body: Retain the main-only rejection, repair the polling deadline, and verify that the separate release-branch procedure covers all supported operator needs.

options.title: Support explicit release targets
options.body: Add a reviewed, opt-in non-main mode with target-ref validation instead of rejecting every release-branch invocation.

recommendation.title: Keep the strict boundary
recommendation.body: Retain the main-only rejection, repair the polling deadline, and verify that the separate release-branch procedure covers all supported operator needs.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to both the release orchestration and the proposed operator-boundary change.
